'''Frederick William Allendorf''' (born April 29, 1947) is an American biologist who is the Regents Professor of Biology Emeritus at the [[University of Montana]]. He has published widely on the topics of [[population genetics]] and [[conservation biology]].<ref name=cv>{{cite web|url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Y2Ap2dTtY4UFoH8cck8xEuC5njswyK9C/view |format=PDF |title=Fred W. Allendorf CV |accessdate=2018-06-07}}</ref><ref name=googlescholar>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=APAWvxsAAAAJ&hl=en |title=Google Scholar Citations}}</ref> Among other organisms, Allendorf has written extensively about [[salmon]].<ref name=googlescholar />

== Early life and education ==
Allendorf was born in [[Philadelphia]]. He earned a Bachelor of Science degree in [[zoology]] from [[Pennsylvania State University]] in 1971.<ref name="cv" /> He then went on to receive his Master of Science in [[fishery|fisheries]] in 1973 and his PhD in fisheries and genetics in 1975, both from the [[University of Washington]].<ref name="cv" />

== Career ==
Before he was a scientist, Allendorf served in the [[United States Army]] from 1965 to 1968 during the [[Vietnam War]].<ref name="cv" /> After he received his PhD he was a postdoctoral scholar at [[Aarhus University]] in Denmark under Freddy B. Christiansen and was later a [[NATO]] Research Fellow at the [[University of Nottingham]] in England under [[Bryan Clarke]].<ref name="cv" /> In 1987, Allendorf was elected as a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref name="cv" /> In 1992, he was elected president of the [[American Genetic Association]].<ref name="cv" />

Allendorf was elected as a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fred W. Allendorf|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/fred-w-allendorf|access-date=2020-06-15|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en}}</ref>

He received the 2015 Molecular Ecology Prize for his contributions to the fields of [[conservation genetics]] and [[molecular ecology]].<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/mec.13503 | doi=10.1111/mec.13503 | title=Recipient of the 2015 ''Molecular Ecology'' Prize: Fred Allendorf | date=2016 | last1=Schwartz | first1=Michael K. | journal=Molecular Ecology | volume=25 | issue=2 | pages=450–453 | pmid=26800037 | bibcode=2016MolEc..25..450S | doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In 2014, Allendorf's wife was killed in an avalanche that also destroyed his home.<ref>{{cite web |date=2015-02-28 |title=A year later, Fred Allendorf struggles to heal from deadly Mount Jumbo avalanche &#124; State and Regional |url=http://helenair.com/news/state-and-regional/a-year-later-fred-allendorf-struggles-to-heal-from-deadly/article_5edd9131-5059-5242-8450-4cd9188a4d40.html |website=Helenair.com |accessdate=2017-03-04}}</ref>
